subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Increasing levels of which gases are linked to global warming?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases whose rising levels are linked to global warming.

questions.q: In the carbon cycle, how is carbon dioxide removed from the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air, using it to make glucose in plants.

questions.q: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi are important because they:
options: Break down dead organisms, recycling nutrients
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead material and waste, recycling nutrients such as carbon and minerals.

questions.q: Which apparatus is used to estimate the number of plants or slow-moving organisms in a sample area?
questions.explain: A quadrat is a square frame placed (often randomly) to count or estimate organisms in a known area.

questions.q: A transect is used in ecological sampling to:
options: Investigate how the distribution of organisms changes across an area
questions.explain: A transect (a line across the habitat) is used to study how species distribution changes, e.g. with distance.

questions.q: What is meant by interdependence in an ecosystem?
options: Species relying on each other for things like food, shelter and pollination
questions.explain: Interdependence means organisms rely on one another (and abiotic factors), so a change in one affects others.

questions.q: In a food chain, what does the direction of the arrows represent?
options: The flow of energy (and biomass) from one organism to the next
questions.explain: Arrows in a food chain show the transfer of energy and biomass from one organism to the next.

questions.q: In a food chain, organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis are called:
questions.explain: Producers, usually green plants and algae, make their own food by photosynthesis and start most food chains.

questions.q: Which factor is an abiotic (non-living) factor affecting an ecosystem?
questions.explain: Light intensity is an abiotic factor; predators, food and disease are biotic (living) factors.

questions.q: Deforestation can harm the environment by:
options: Reducing biodiversity and increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide
Removing carbon dioxide from the air
questions.explain: Deforestation reduces habitats and biodiversity, and means less CO2 is absorbed, contributing to global warming.

questions.q: High biodiversity in an ecosystem is beneficial because it:
options: Reduces the number of food chains
Makes ecosystems more stable and resilient
questions.explain: High biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable, as species are less dependent on any single one.

questions.q: In the water cycle, water returns to the atmosphere mainly through:
questions.explain: Water enters the atmosphere by evaporation from water bodies and transpiration from plants.
